title: Factorization criterion for henselian pairs
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal. Then $(A,I)$ is henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] (for every finite $A$-algebra $B$ every idempotent of $B/IB$ lifts uniquely to an idempotent of $B$) if and only if (i) $I$ is contained in the Jacobson radical of $A$, and (ii) for every monic polynomial $f\in A[T]$ and every factorization $\overline f=g_0h_0$ of its reduction $\overline f\in(A/I)[T]$ into monic polynomials $g_0,h_0\in(A/I)[T]$ generating the unit ideal of $(A/I)[T]$, there are monic polynomials $g,h\in A[T]$ with $f=gh$ whose reductions modulo $I$ are $g_0$ and $h_0$. In particular, if $I$ is contained in the Jacobson radical of $A$, then $(A,I)$ is henselian if and only if (ii) holds.

source.place: Lemma Tag 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair, line 2553), equivalence (3)$\Leftrightarrow$(1): (3) is the definition [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] (idempotents of $B/IB$ lift bijectively for finite $B$), (1) is Stacks' Definition Tag 09XE (definition-henselian-pair, line 2394) = conditions (i) and (ii); proof of 09XI: (3)$\Rightarrow$(1) directly, (1)$\Rightarrow$(5)$\Rightarrow$(2)$\Rightarrow$(4)$\Rightarrow$(3)

proof.text: *(3)$\Rightarrow$(1), part (i): $I$ lies in the Jacobson radical.* Assume $(A,I)$ is henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Let $\mathfrak m$ be a maximal ideal of $A$ and suppose $I\not\subseteq\mathfrak m$; then $I+\mathfrak m=A$. The ring $B=A/(I\cap\mathfrak m)$ is a finite (cyclic) $A$-algebra, and by the Chinese remainder theorem ($I$, $\mathfrak m$ comaximal) $B\cong A/I\times A/\mathfrak m$. Under this isomorphism the image of $I$ is $0\times(I+\mathfrak m)/\mathfrak m=0\times A/\mathfrak m$, so $B/IB\cong A/I$ and $B\to B/IB$ is the first projection. The idempotents $(1,1)$ and $(1,0)$ of $B$ are distinct ($A/\mathfrak m\neq0$) and both map to $1$, contradicting the uniqueness of lifts in the definition. Hence $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$ for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, i.e. (i).

source.place: Lemma Tag 09XI, proof, paragraph 'Assume (3). Let $\mathfrak m$ be a maximal ideal and consider the finite map $A\to B=A/(I\cap\mathfrak m)$ ... Thus we see that $I$ is contained in the Jacobson radical of $A$'

proof.text: *(3)$\Rightarrow$(1), part (ii): factorizations lift.* Assume $(A,I)$ henselian; by step 1, $I$ lies in the Jacobson radical. Let $f\in A[T]$ be monic and $\overline f=g_0h_0$ with $g_0,h_0$ monic generating the unit ideal of $(A/I)[T]$. Put $B=A[T]/(f)$: a free $A$-module with basis $1,T,\dots,T^{\deg f-1}$, hence a finite $A$-algebra, with $B/IB\cong(A/I)[T]/(\overline f)$ [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free]. As the ideals $(g_0)$, $(h_0)$ of $(A/I)[T]$ are comaximal, $(g_0)\cap(h_0)=(g_0h_0)=(\overline f)$ and the Chinese remainder theorem gives $B/IB\cong(A/I)[T]/(g_0)\times(A/I)[T]/(h_0)$; let $\bar e\in B/IB$ be the idempotent corresponding to $(1,0)$. By the definition of henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] applied to the finite $A$-algebra $B$ there is an idempotent $e\in B$ lifting $\bar e$. By [lem-weil-pbc-idempotent-splitting-monic-factorization] (its hypotheses: $I$ in the Jacobson radical, $f$, $g_0$, $h_0$, $\bar e$, $e$ as here) there are monic $g,h\in A[T]$ with $f=gh$ and reductions $g_0$, $h_0$. This is (ii).

source.place: Lemma Tag 09XI, proof, paragraph 'Assume (3)', from 'Let $f\in A[T]$ be monic' to 'Thus (3) implies (1)'

proof.text: *(1)$\Rightarrow$(5): Gabber's root condition.* Assume (i) and (ii). Let $f(T)=T^n(T-1)+a_nT^n+\dots+a_1T+a_0$ with $n\ge1$ and $a_0,\dots,a_n\in I$; $f$ is monic of degree $n+1$ and $\overline f=T^n(T-1)$. The monic polynomials $g_0=T^n$, $h_0=T-1$ generate the unit ideal: $1=T^n-(T-1)(T^{n-1}+\dots+T+1)$. By (ii), $f=gh$ with $g,h\in A[T]$ monic, $\overline g=T^n$, $\overline h=T-1$. If $A/I=0$, then $1\in I$ lies in the Jacobson radical by (i), so $A$ has no maximal ideal, $A=0$, and $\alpha=0$ is a root of $f$ in $1+I=A$. Otherwise the reduction of a monic polynomial is monic of the same degree, so $\deg h=1$, $h=T-\alpha$ with $\alpha\equiv1$ modulo $I$, and $f(\alpha)=g(\alpha)h(\alpha)=0$. So every such $f$ has a root in $1+I$, and $I$ lies in the Jacobson radical by (i): this is condition (5) of 09XI.

source.place: Lemma Tag 09XI, proof, paragraph 'Assume (1). Let $f$ be as in (5) ... Thus (1) implies (5)'

proof.text: *(5)$\Rightarrow$(2): sections of etale algebras lift.* By step 3, $I$ lies in the Jacobson radical and every polynomial $T^n(T-1)+a_nT^n+\dots+a_0$ ($n\ge1$, $a_i\in I$) has a root in $1+I$. By [lem-weil-pbc-gabber-root-criterion-etale-section-lifting], for every ring map $A\to A'$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A'\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ etale and every $A$-algebra map $\sigma:A'\to A/I$ there is an $A$-algebra map $\tau:A'\to A$ lifting $\sigma$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 09XI, proof, paragraphs from 'Assume (5). We will show that (2) holds' to the end of the proof

proof.text: *(2)$\Rightarrow$(4)$\Rightarrow$(3): $(A,I)$ is henselian.* By step 4 the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-lifting-henselian-pair] holds, so $(A,I)$ is henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]: for every finite $A$-algebra $B$ every idempotent of $B/IB$ lifts uniquely to an idempotent of $B$. With steps 1-2 this proves the equivalence.

source.place: Lemma Tag 09XI, proof, first paragraph 'Assume (2) ... In this way we see that (2) implies (4)' and 'The implication (4)$\Rightarrow$(3) is trivial'

proof.text: *The particular case.* If $I$ lies in the Jacobson radical, condition (i) holds, so the equivalence of steps 1-5 reads: $(A,I)$ henselian if and only if (ii).
